DRAFT → QUOTED → PENDING_PAYMENT → CONFIRMED → FULFILLING → FULFILLED
  └──────────────→ CANCELLED        ↘ CANCEL_REQUESTED ↘ PARTIALLY_FULFILLED
CONFIRMED/FULFILLING/FULFILLED → RETURN_OR_REFUND_PENDING → PARTIALLY_REFUNDED/REFUNDED
                                       ↘ DISPUTED (separate case lifecycle)

Назви залежать від domain, але legal transition table має source, event, target, guard, reason code, actor, state-machine version і side effects. Terminal/nonterminal задаються explicitly: наприклад CANCELLED terminal для fulfillment, але refund/dispute record може ще жити; PENDING_PAYMENT nonterminal. Fulfillment не виводиться лише з payment state: policy може вимагати capture, fraud review або inventory. Server CAS/version/transaction enforce transition and invariants; client reducer лише project-ить.

Payment state machine

CREATED → REQUIRES_METHOD → REQUIRES_ACTION → PROCESSING
   ├→ DECLINED / CANCELLED / EXPIRED
   └→ AUTHORIZED → CAPTURE_PENDING → PARTIALLY_CAPTURED → CAPTURED → SETTLED
                     └→ VOIDED              └→ REFUND_PENDING → PARTIALLY_REFUNDED → REFUNDED
CAPTURED/SETTLED → DISPUTED → WON/LOST (conceptual provider/rail case)

Provider capabilities differ: authorization/capture may be immediate, delayed, partial or unsupported; void usually addresses an uncaptured authorization, refund a captured payment. Decline, cancellation, expiry, void, refund and dispute have stable internal reason categories plus redacted provider code. Do not invent universal provider transitions. HTTP 2xx means request-level success only; provider acceptance is not authorization, authorization is not capture, capture is not settlement, and none alone proves fulfillment/business success. Every transition validates amount/currency, cumulative capture ≤ authorized, cumulative refund ≤ captured (under agreed fee/rail semantics), version and legal predecessor server-side.

Checkout sequence

  1. Client requests checkout with cart version; backend authenticates account, reloads catalog facts, revalidates price/tax/promotion/shipping/inventory, reserves stock with expiry, and returns a versioned quote.
  2. On explicit user confirmation, client submits stable business operation key + quote/version. Backend transaction creates order snapshot, PENDING_PAYMENT, idempotency record and durable outbox intent.
  3. Backend creates provider payment intent/session using server-held credentials and its supported idempotency semantics; hosted/provider UI or tokenization keeps raw card entry away from app/backend where feasible.
  4. Client presents provider UI. Browser/3DS/external app may kill/recreate process. Persist only safe order/session reference; restore by backend status, never by trusting UI callback.
  5. Backend verifies provider status/webhook, applies payment transition, commits order transition and outbox. Fulfillment consumes durable confirmed policy event, not return URL.
  6. Client observes/polls backend order. Only backend durable state may show confirmed; receipt/support path includes order ID, not secrets.

Redirect, process-death, and ambiguous recovery

Deep link/app link carries opaque correlation/state, not amount or authorization. Validate scheme/host/path, one-time nonce/state binding, account/session, expiry and expected order; reject replay/tampering. A return URL is a hint only. After timeout, app death, browser/3DS/external-app redirect or provider success with lost response, mark UNKNOWN/PENDING_RECONCILIATION, query backend by operation/order ID, and backend verifies with provider. Never start a fresh payment blindly. Local optimistic order state is provisional. Client clock cannot decide expiry; use backend/provider state and authoritative timestamps.

Idempotency contract

A stable operation key identifies one business operation such as “submit quote v7 for account X,” and is reused across the same retry/recovery. Server atomically stores scope/principal + key + payload fingerprint + API/semantic version + status/result and replays the same response. Same key/different fingerprint is conflict, not a new charge. Define endpoint/provider scope, concurrency behavior, TTL/retention and what happens after expiry/version change. A client UUID alone and retries alone do not guarantee dedupe. Idempotency narrows duplicates only when server/provider semantics implement it; exactly-once end-to-end cannot be assumed.

Webhooks, inbox, and reconciliation

Authenticate webhook per provider's current documented scheme: verify signature/key/secret, raw-body/canonicalization and timestamp/replay window exactly as specified—do not invent crypto rules. Rotate keys by provider guidance. Persist an inbox/event ledger before processing; dedupe by provider+event ID. Expect duplicate, out-of-order and missing events. Event creation timestamp alone is not authority for rollback; fetch current provider object/version when needed, apply legal monotonic transitions, and record ignored/conflicting reason.

Fast receipt/ACK is transport handling, not settlement. Durable worker processes inbox; polling/status lookup and scheduled reconciliation repair missing webhooks and ambiguous old states. Metrics include webhook lag, signature failures, duplicates, oldest unprocessed inbox, unknown-state age and reconciliation mismatches.

Atomicity, saga, inventory, and compensation

A Room transaction, backend DB transaction and provider operation are not one distributed transaction. Use a saga: durable local/server state, outbox before external call, idempotent step, inbox/result, next transition; compensation such as release reservation, void authorization or initiate refund is itself fallible and tracked—not rollback magic. Inventory reservation has owner, quantity, authoritative expiry and release; late capture after expiry needs explicit policy. Strong reservation reduces oversell but lowers availability/utilization; optimistic stock improves conversion but risks backorder. Server revalidates price, tax, promotion, shipping and inventory at commitment boundaries; client cart is not authority.

Offline, PCI, and mobile security boundaries

Browsing/cart may work offline; payment confirmation needs backend/provider. Never queue a payment invisibly as ordinary background retry. WorkManager is not an exact scheduler and should not own silent payment retries; it may refresh visible pending status/reconciliation with safe idempotent reads under policy. Require a fresh explicit user action if a new charge operation is needed.

Minimize PCI scope: prefer provider-hosted UI/components or platform billing and provider tokenization; custom PAN entry expands scope and operational burden. Never store/log raw PAN or CVV; CVV must not be retained after authorization even encrypted, and the safer mobile design avoids receiving it outside approved provider UI. Tokens are scoped references, not universally harmless data. TLS protects transport, not compromised endpoints or business correctness. Android Keystore can protect non-exportable key material/use, but does not make plaintext safe while legitimately used and does not authorize backend actions. Obfuscation/encryption do not turn shipped secrets into secrets; provider secret keys stay backend-side.

Observability, audit, and support

Propagate correlation ID, client operation ID, order ID, payment-attempt ID and provider reference. Transition ledger records from/to/version/reason/actor/source/event, amount/currency and redacted evidence. Logs never include PAN/CVV/token/secret/full webhook body/PII; auditability is balanced against data minimization, access control and retention/deletion law. Dashboards: payment state funnel by allowed dimensions, ambiguous count/age, authorization→capture age, reservation expiry/release, webhook lag/inbox age, dedupe conflicts, reconciliation mismatch, refund age, fulfillment-after-cancel and support cases. Support tooling shows safe timeline and controlled retry/reconcile/refund actions with authorization and audit.

Reliability, security, and testing

Backend enforces authenticated account partitioning/ownership, amount/currency/quote version, rate limits and conceptual replay/fraud controls; never trust client/provider redirect fields. Use fake provider with deterministic clock plus provider contract/sandbox tests. Test duplicate/reordered/dropped webhooks; timeout after provider success; app/process death during challenge; redirect replay/tamper; concurrent same/different idempotency payload; authorization/capture/void; partial capture/refund; dispute; reconciliation; inventory expiry/oversell; Room/backend migrations; old/new state-machine versions; property/model tests that every generated transition preserves money/order invariants. Sandbox proves integration shape, not production rail behavior.

Failure matrix

FailureState/responseRepair
Offline before confirmationCart retained; no success/charge queuedUser resumes explicit checkout online
Timeout after provider successUNKNOWN, do not create new attemptSame key + backend/provider lookup/reconcile
Process death in 3DS/browserSafe order reference onlyReturn hint then backend verification
Duplicate/out-of-order webhookInbox dedupe/legal transition guardFetch provider current state
Missing webhookState age alarmPolling/reconciliation
Reservation expiresNo silent fulfillmentReprice/re-reserve/cancel or explicit policy
Capture succeeds, DB write failsAmbiguous durable provider effectProvider query + inbox/reconcile, then order transition
Refund succeeds, response lostREFUND_PENDING/UNKNOWNReuse refund operation key/status lookup
Account switch/replayReject partition mismatchFence local work; server ownership check
Currency/amount mismatchFail closedRecreate from authoritative quote

Guarantees and non-guarantees

  • Exactly-once end-to-end cannot be assumed; idempotency narrows duplicates only with implemented server/provider semantics.
  • Payment UI success is not durable order confirmation; local optimistic order state is provisional.
  • Webhook receipt is not necessarily settlement; HTTP 2xx/provider acceptance/authorization/capture/settlement/fulfillment/business success differ.
  • Room, backend DB and provider are separate atomicity boundaries; saga compensation can also fail.
  • WorkManager is not an exact scheduler and must not own silent payment retries.
  • Return URL/deep link is a hint; backend/provider verification is authority.
  • Clock/client timestamps are not authoritative.
  • Refunds do not instantly erase settlement/fulfillment effects.
  • TLS/Keystore/obfuscation do not make shipped secrets or a compromised endpoint safe.
  • Play Billing and payments policy are version/region/distribution sensitive; verify current official guidance.

Decision framework

  1. Classify product/rail and current policy: digital vs physical/service, region/distribution, authorization/capture/refund needs.
  2. Define user journeys, money/inventory/fulfillment invariants, terminal states and false-success cost.
  3. Draw cart→quote→order and separate payment state machines; name every authority and atomic boundary.
  4. Select hosted/provider UI versus custom entry by UX, capability and PCI/security scope—not aesthetics alone.
  5. Specify idempotency, ambiguous recovery, webhook inbox/reconciliation and reservation/compensation.
  6. Finish with account authorization, audit/privacy, support, metrics, failure matrix, tests and versioned evolution.

Trade-offs and evolution

Hosted UI/tokenization minimizes card-data exposure but limits styling/control; custom entry raises PCI/security/testing burden. Immediate capture simplifies flow but weakens cancel-before-fulfillment flexibility; delayed capture risks auth expiry and needs reconciliation. Strong inventory reservation reduces oversell but ties stock; optimistic inventory improves availability but increases backorder/compensation. Longer idempotency/event retention improves replay repair but costs privacy/storage. Polling repairs missing webhooks but costs provider quota. Evolve via versioned state/event schemas, additive fields, tolerant readers, expand-contract DB migration, dual-read/shadow reconciliation and measured cutover; never reinterpret old terminal states silently.

Production incident

Після 3DS provider авторизував платіж, але mobile return загубився. App timeout позначив attempt failed, WorkManager мовчки створив новий UUID і повторив charge; webhook другого платежу прийшов раніше першого. Два captures, один order. Containment: stop silent retries, mark affected orders unknown, query provider by merchant/order references, void/refund duplicates with support audit. Root cause: UI callback був authority, keys були per-attempt, inbox не guard-ив legal transitions. Fix: stable business key+fingerprint and response replay, backend status authority, event inbox/reconciliation, separate states and ambiguity-age alerts.

Code-review/design trap

Trap: Double total, client sends amount, app stores card data encrypted in Room, marks PAID on provider UI callback, and OneTimeWorkRequest retries charge with a fresh UUID. Це допускає rounding drift, tampering, PCI expansion, false confirmation і duplicate charges. Replace with Money currency+minor units/exact decimal, server quote/order snapshot, provider-hosted tokenization, stable operation key+fingerprint, backend verification and explicit unknown/reconcile path.

Likely practice Q&A

Це likely practice questions, не підтверджений і не гарантований список співбесіди.

  1. Q: З чого почати payment design? A: Product/rail/policy, journeys, money/inventory invariants, failure cost and authorities.
  2. Q: Cart, order і payment — одне? A: Ні: mutable intent, commercial snapshot/lifecycle і money workflow мають окремі identities/states.
  3. Q: Як model money? A: Integer minor units або exact decimal + currency + explicit scale/rounding, never binary float.
  4. Q: Коли показати confirmed? A: Лише після durable backend order state; UI/provider callback є hint.
  5. Q: Як уникнути duplicate charge? A: Stable business key, server record/fingerprint/replay, provider semantics і reconciliation.
  6. Q: Що робити після timeout? A: UNKNOWN; lookup by same operation/order, verify provider, не blind new charge.
  7. Q: Чи webhook є truth? A: Authenticated input; dedupe/inbox/legal transition, current-state fetch і reconciliation.
  8. Q: Де atomic transaction? A: Окремо Room, backend DB і provider; saga/outbox/inbox bridge, compensation tracked.
  9. Q: Offline payment? A: Browse/cart можуть; confirmation needs backend/provider and no invisible queued charge.
  10. Q: Як тестувати? A: Fake provider, sandbox/contracts, failures/reorder/duplicates/process death, model/invariant/migration tests.

Senior follow-ups

  1. Спроєктуйте split shipment із delayed/partial capture, auth expiry та partial cancellation.
  2. Визначте idempotency scope/TTL/version migration, коли mobile client живе довше server release.
  3. Побудуйте reconciliation для missing/out-of-order webhooks без unsafe state regression.
  4. Порівняйте inventory reserve-before-pay і pay-before-reserve за oversell/abandonment/compensation.

Unanswered self-checks

  1. Який exact durable fact дозволяє fulfillment, і що забороняє його двічі?
  2. Як довести outcome, якщо process помер між provider success і backend commit?
  3. Які idempotency scope, fingerprint, retention та expired-key semantics?
  4. Які payment/audit data справді потрібні, хто має access і коли вони видаляються?

English answer skeletons

30-second answer

“I start by classifying digital versus physical goods and current store/payment policy, then define money, inventory, order, fulfillment and refund invariants. Cart, order and payment are separate models and order/payment have separate server-enforced state machines. The backend owns amount, currency, authorization and durable confirmation; hosted provider UI minimizes PCI scope. A stable business idempotency key, inbox/outbox and reconciliation handle duplicate and ambiguous outcomes. A UI success or webhook receipt is not final business success.”

2-minute answer

“I ask about product type, region/distribution policy, authorization versus capture, partial shipment/refund, scale, inventory contention, offline UX and audit retention. Money uses minor units or exact decimal with currency and explicit rounding, never binary floating point. The server revalidates cart prices, tax, promotions, shipping and stock and creates an immutable order snapshot plus reservation. Order and payment have independent versioned state machines with legal transitions, reason codes and server-side invariants. A stable operation key is bound to principal, payload fingerprint and semantic version; the server stores and replays the result, while provider idempotency is used where documented. Hosted/provider UI tokenizes data and keeps raw PAN/CVV away; TLS, Keystore and obfuscation are not backend authorization or secret storage. Redirects are hints: after 3DS, timeout or process death, the app queries backend and the backend verifies provider state. Signed webhooks enter a deduplicating inbox; duplicates, reordering and loss are repaired by monotonic transition guards, polling and reconciliation. Room, backend DB and provider cannot share one transaction, so durable outbox/inbox and a saga track compensation, inventory release, void or refund. I expose provisional local states honestly, never silently retry a charge with WorkManager, and test fake-provider contracts, timeout-after-success, duplicate/reordered/missing webhooks, process death, refunds, migrations and state-machine properties.”

Official references

  • Google Play — Payments policy; Android Developers — Play Billing; Integrate Play Billing; Backend integration
  • PCI SSC — Tokenization Guidelines; PCI SSC — Data storage do’s and don’ts; PCI SSC — Card verification code FAQ
  • Android Developers — Android Keystore; Security best practices; WorkManager task scheduling
  • EMVCo — EMV 3-D Secure; IETF RFC 9110 — HTTP semantics
System design: auth, analytics and feature flagsрозгорнути / згорнути

Мета і senior mental model

Спроєктувати три окремі, але інтегровані platform subsystems: auth встановлює session context, analytics асинхронно вимірює дозволені факти, feature flags постачають versioned policy snapshot. Це cross-cutting design, не один «SDK manager»: окремі owners, storage, failure domains, privacy/security contracts і data/control planes. Stage 30 не занурюється в Stage 31 migration-program чи Stage 32 leadership depth.

Requirements and ownership checklist

  • Auth owner: identity-provider/backend contract, redirect registration, token/session lifecycle, account partitioning, revocation incident path; mobile owner — external-user-agent integration, local session state, secure-use boundary та UX.
  • Analytics owner: product taxonomy/schema registry, consent purpose, retention/deletion, ingestion/data quality і consumers; mobile owner — validation, queue, upload і context snapshot.
  • Flags owner: typed registry, owner/purpose/default/expiry, rollout/experiment policy, invariants і removal; mobile owner — validated snapshot, safe fallback та exposure integration.
  • Shared requirements: anonymous/signed-in journeys, multi-account/logout, cold start/process death/offline, accessibility, latency/battery/storage/network budgets, supported versions/providers, threat model, audit, incident rollback і testability. Зафіксуйте SLO/quotas як product variables, не вигадані constants.

Architecture, dependency graph and data flow

build config ───────────────→ safe local defaults
                                  ↓
Keystore-backed key use → Auth/session owner → immutable Context(account/session/device*)
         ↕ IdP/browser          ↓                    ↘
backend auth/resource APIs ← token coordinator       Flag client ← control plane
         │                       │                    ↓ validated snapshot
         └──── authorization ────┴→ product features ─┬→ exposure decision
                                                     ↓
consent → event API → schema/PII validator → durable bounded queue → uploader
                                                     ↓
                      analytics ingestion validation/dedupe → warehouse
separate observability pipeline ← health/latency/errors (redacted)

device* означає privacy-appropriate pseudonymous app-instance identifier, не hardware identity. Dependency direction: мінімальний local config → auth restore → consent/context → validated flag snapshot → features; analytics не блокує auth або essential UI. Control-plane outage (flags/analytics configuration) не має зупиняти data-plane auth/resource calls; feedback loop «analytics green → rollout grows» потребує independent guardrails, бо telemetry loss може виглядати як health.

AUTH — vocabulary, OAuth 2/OIDC and trust boundaries

Identity — subject/account representation; authentication — evidence that establishes a principal/session; authorization — server decision for a resource/action; session — bounded authenticated continuity; account — product/tenant data boundary; device/app instance — execution/routing context, not a person. OAuth 2 is delegated authorization framework; OIDC adds identity claims/ID token and discovery. Access token calls a resource server; refresh token obtains new tokens; ID token is not a generic API bearer token.

Native apps use Authorization Code + PKCE through an external user-agent (browser/Custom Tabs or provider-supported system flow), not embedded WebView for general OAuth login. Generate high-entropy code_verifier, send derived challenge, retain verifier only for that transaction. Validate exact registered redirect URI/App Link, verified HTTPS association where supported, expected issuer/client, one-time state binding and OIDC nonce; authorization server validates code, redirect and PKCE, backend/resource server validates signature/issuer/audience/expiry/scopes and performs authorization. PKCE does not replace redirect, state, nonce, issuer/audience/scope or server validation. No client secret shipped in APK: TLS and obfuscation do not make shipped secrets safe.

AUTH — tokens, refresh, errors and session state machine

SIGNED_OUT → AUTHORIZING(state, nonce, verifier) → EXCHANGING → ACTIVE
    ↑              ↘ CANCELLED/REDIRECT_REJECTED       ↓ expiry/401
    └ REVOKED/LOGOUT ← AUTH_BLOCKED ← REFRESHING(single-flight)
                              ↘ TRANSIENT_OFFLINE (qualified cached UX)

Prefer short-lived access tokens. Refresh-token rotation and reuse detection are authorization-server/provider policies, not a client-created guarantee. A token coordinator snapshots token generation; concurrent 401s join one single-flight refresh (Mutex/shared Deferred), then eligible callers retry exactly once only if request semantics are safe/replayable. HTTP 401 retry is unsafe for arbitrary non-idempotent operations; use endpoint idempotency/status reconciliation. A 401 is authentication/session evidence; 403 is authorization denial and normally not refreshable; timeout/DNS/5xx is transient network/service failure and must not silently sign out. Account-disabled/consent-required/provider codes need explicit mapping.

Use token expiry with bounded server/provider guidance for clock skew and a monotonic elapsed timer only within the same boot where appropriate; local wall clock is not authority. Refresh failure taxonomy distinguishes invalid/revoked credential from transient reachability. Connectivity callback does not prove backend reachability. Offline UX may expose qualified cached data while marking session unverified; sensitive mutations wait for backend authorization.

AUTH — storage, accounts, logout and platform APIs

Partition token set, generation, caches, queues and work by immutable account/tenant key. On account switch: fence old generation, cancel requests/work, clear memory, detach observers, activate target partition, then rebuild context; never execute account A work as B. Logout clears local tokens/keys/data per policy, cancels work, resets flags/context and requests provider/backend revocation where supported. Logout cannot guarantee immediate invalidation without server support; already processed requests remain, access tokens may live until expiry, and other devices require server session controls.

Android Keystore can keep key material non-exportable and gate key use under its threat model; it does not protect plaintext after legitimate use, logs, screenshots, memory, accessibility abuse, or a compromised unlocked runtime. Biometric is a local user-presence/key-use gate, not proof of remote identity or backend authorization. Credential Manager/passkeys provide conceptual credential mediation and public-key authentication, but availability, API shape, provider behavior, restore/sync and fallback are Android/Jetpack/Play-services/provider/version-sensitive: follow current official docs and backend ceremony validation. Do not invent a universal passkey UX or store a client secret.

ANALYTICS — taxonomy, schema and identity

Use a reviewed schema registry: stable semantic event name, version, purpose/owner, required/optional typed fields, allowed enums/ranges, PII classification, retention and deprecation. Prefer business facts (checkout_submitted) over widget names. Source timestamp records client observation; ingestion timestamp records server receipt. Event timestamp is not trusted global order. Envelope may contain event ID, schema version, source time, session ID and privacy-approved pseudonymous user/app-instance IDs; do not use raw email/phone/ad ID by default. Anonymous→signed-in transition links only through an explicit privacy/backend policy; never unsafe-merge profiles merely because one device logged in.

Consent is purpose-specific state, not one boolean. Data minimization precedes collection; a PII denylist catches known hazards but an explicit field allowlist/schema is the positive boundary. Never include access/refresh tokens, authorization headers, credential payloads, payment/chat content or arbitrary exception/request bodies. Local validation rejects/quarantines malformed/unknown fields; server ingestion revalidates schema, size, tenant, consent metadata and abuse limits.

ANALYTICS — queue, delivery and data quality

CREATED → VALIDATED → PERSISTED → BATCHED → IN_FLIGHT → ACKED → DELETED
             ↘ DROPPED(policy/schema/consent/quota)
PERSISTED/IN_FLIGHT → RETRY_WAIT(backoff+jitter) → BATCHED
corrupt/full → QUARANTINE or bounded DROP with health counter

Persist before scheduling when durability is required; use bounded queue/bytes/age, batch limits, compression, authenticated upload, exponential backoff with jitter, server Retry-After, network/battery constraints and quotas/backpressure. Sampling happens under documented policy before or with weights; never sample mandatory audit/security data into product analytics. At-least-once-oriented retry can duplicate: stable event ID permits ingestion dedupe within documented retention, but delivery, order and exactly-once are not guaranteed. Preserve local sequence only as diagnostic/session hint; batches can be late, duplicate or out of order after offline/retry. Server consumers use event IDs, ingestion partitions and business versions rather than trusting source timestamps as global order.

Schema evolution is additive/versioned with tolerant readers, dual validation and deprecation telemetry; meaning changes require a new event/version, not silent reuse. Data-quality owner monitors reject/unknown/duplicate/late rates, required-field nulls, cardinality, volume and producer version. Product analytics remains separate from operational observability: crash/latency/queue health has different purpose, access, retention and sampling.

FEATURE FLAGS / REMOTE CONFIG — registry and snapshot

Typed registry entry: key/type, owner, purpose, safe local default, allowed range, expiry/removal issue, dependencies/invariants, audience, privacy classification and whether it is an experiment/kill switch. Build-time config selects immutable endpoint/environment/capability and must not contain secrets; runtime config tunes behavior within a shipped safe envelope. Flags are neither authorization nor secret storage, and auth state must not be controlled solely by Remote Config.

LOCAL_DEFAULT → CACHE_LOADED(last-known-good) → FETCHING → FETCHED_UNVALIDATED
       ↑                  ↑                         ↓ validate schema/type/version/invariants
       └ FALLBACK/REJECTED ← MALFORMED          ACTIVATED(snapshotVersion)
ACTIVE → STALE_OFFLINE; next valid activation atomically replaces whole snapshot

Separate fetch from activate: fetch success does not imply activation or valid business invariants. Validate signature/transport/provider contract as applicable, schema, types, ranges, dependencies and mutually exclusive states, then atomically publish immutable snapshot; retain last-known-good plus local default. Cache expiration/min-fetch intervals and real-time update APIs are provider/version-sensitive. Real-time config is not hard real-time; stale flags may persist offline or until process/fetch/activation, so an offline kill switch cannot guarantee immediate effect.

FEATURE FLAGS — targeting, experiments and safety

Provider/server-side targeting can return evaluated values while some systems expose client-visible rules/parameters; assume a motivated client can inspect or alter any shipped/evaluated client state. Deterministic bucketing hashes experiment/flag ID (або salt)+stable privacy-appropriate unit key у фіксований bucket range зі specified algorithm, а allocation мапить buckets на variants; зміна key або salt перетасовує assignments (churn). Sticky assignment persisted/server-owned can reduce churn but complicates deletion, cross-device consistency and experiment contamination. Deterministic bucketing does not guarantee statistically valid experiments: allocation, eligibility, sample-ratio mismatch, interference, novelty and analysis still matter.

Emit experiment exposure only when the user actually receives/renders the treatment (or crosses the precisely defined exposure boundary), not at fetch, activate, assignment or app startup. Include experiment/variant/snapshot attribution consistently. Staged rollout uses cohorts, guardrails and stop criteria; kill switch has safe default/LKG semantics; circuit breaker/fallback protects a failing data-plane dependency without trusting analytics alone. Validate dependencies (A requires B), invariants and unsupported combinations before activation. Expired flags fail CI/registry review, are disabled, code paths removed, analytics retired and server key deleted to control flag debt.

Integration: startup, logout, account switch and consent

Cold start/process death/offline: (1) load immutable build config/local defaults; (2) open account-partitioned encrypted-as-designed stores and recover queue integrity; (3) restore auth metadata/token handle without assuming validity; (4) load consent; (5) load and validate LKG flag snapshot for anonymous/account context; (6) publish one immutable context generation; (7) start features; (8) asynchronously refresh session/config and upload eligible analytics. Network failures degrade independently.

Logout: bump generation/fence calls → cancel/join refresh and account work → revoke server/provider if reachable → clear local credentials and sensitive account data → purge or reclassify queued events by consent/retention policy → reset flags to anonymous safe snapshot → publish signed-out context. Account switch: perform old-account teardown, never merge profiles, then open target partition and fetch target session/flags. Consent withdrawal: stop new collection immediately for that purpose, delete/quarantine local queued data, propagate backend deletion request/status and reset identifiers as policy requires; local deletion alone does not satisfy backend deletion.

Every request/event/exposure captures a consistent context generation (account pseudonym, session, consent version, flag snapshot/experiment) rather than reading mutable globals field-by-field. Analytics must not gate auth availability; flags failure must not erase auth; auth transition rotates account-scoped analytics/flag context without unsafe anonymous-profile merge.

Failure matrix

FailureClassification / safe responseRepair / evidence
Redirect replay/tamperAuthentication transaction rejected; consume state onceValidate URI/state/nonce/verifier/issuer; audit redacted reason
Concurrent 401 stormOne refresh; waiters retry once only if safeGeneration/single-flight metrics and MockWebServer race test
403Authorization failure, no refresh loopBackend policy/support path
Timeout/5xx/offlineTransient, keep qualified session/cache; no forced logoutBackoff/jitter and reachability probe
Token revokedAUTH_BLOCKED/signed out for affected sessionClear/fence and explicit re-auth
Queue corrupt/full diskQuarantine/drop by bounded policy; product flow continuesIntegrity recovery, counters, storage pressure test
Consent withdrawnStop purpose collection; local purgeBackend deletion workflow with auditable status
Schema mismatchClient reject/quarantine; ingestion rejectRegistry compatibility and producer alert
Duplicate/reordered uploadDedupe window; no source-time ordering claimEvent IDs/version-aware consumer
Stale/malformed flagsReject candidate; LKG/local defaultSnapshot validation and age alarm
Kill switch while offlineStale value may persistSafety built into local default/circuit breaker; reconnect refresh
Flag dependency violationReject entire snapshot/fail closed for risky featureInvariant test and owner alert

Guarantees and non-guarantees

  • PKCE does not replace redirect/state/nonce/issuer/audience/scope/server validation.
  • Keystore protects key material under its threat model, not a compromised unlocked runtime; TLS/obfuscation do not make shipped secrets safe.
  • Logout cannot guarantee immediate invalidation without server support; 401 retry is unsafe for arbitrary non-idempotent operations.
  • Connectivity callback does not prove backend reachability.
  • Analytics delivery, order and exactly-once are not guaranteed; source event timestamp is not trusted global order.
  • Local deletion does not itself satisfy backend deletion.
  • Remote Config fetch success does not imply activation or valid business invariants; stale flags may persist offline and real-time config is not hard real-time.
  • Flags cannot enforce authorization or protect secrets; auth state cannot depend solely on a flag.
  • Deterministic bucketing does not guarantee statistically valid experiments.
  • CI green does not prove privacy/compliance.

API/provider/version-sensitive guidance

Pin and verify current Android/Jetpack/provider docs for Credential Manager/passkeys, biometric authenticator/key invalidation, Keystore capabilities, verified App Links, Custom Tabs, backup/restore and process/background behavior. OAuth/OIDC discovery, token rotation/reuse, revocation, logout, passkey ceremony and refresh semantics are IdP/backend contracts. Remote Config min-fetch/cache/real-time activation and Analytics upload limits/consent APIs vary by SDK/provider/version; wrap them behind your contracts and test pinned versions. Server validates authorization, token audience/scope, schemas, quotas and deletion regardless of client SDK.

Decisions, trade-offs and evolution

Longer sessions improve continuity but enlarge revocation window; stronger local presence gates add friction without replacing server identity. Durable analytics improves offline coverage but costs storage/privacy and increases late duplicates; aggressive sampling lowers cost but weakens cohort analysis. LKG flags improve availability but retain stale risk; local safe defaults reduce blast radius but may disable value. Sticky assignments reduce churn but complicate deletion/cross-device semantics. Evolve via versioned auth/session contracts, additive event schemas, typed flag registry, capability negotiation, shadow validation and measured rollout; do not silently reinterpret old events or token/account partitions.

Observability, testing, privacy and security

Separate redacted operational metrics: auth state/refresh waiters/outcome/latency, redirect rejects, 401 vs 403 vs transient errors; analytics queue bytes/age/drop/reject/duplicate/late/upload latency; flag snapshot version/age/fetch-vs-activate/reject reason/exposure and dependency failures. Bound cardinality; no tokens, raw IDs, payloads or PII. Audit access, retention/deletion and sampling; privacy/security review data flows and threat model, not only code.

Deterministic tests with fake clock/IdP/ingestion/config plus real storage fixtures cover: concurrent refresh and one safe retry; redirect replay/tamper; process death during auth/queue/fetch; account switch and stale-generation fencing; token revocation; queue corruption/full storage; consent withdrawal plus backend deletion workflow; schema mismatch; duplicate/reordered/late upload; stale/malformed config; deterministic bucketing vectors and key change; offline kill switch; dependency/invariant rejection. Add contract tests for audience/scope, event registry/ingestion, provider APIs; property/state-machine tests; upgrade/backup fixtures; end-to-end privacy assertions. CI green is evidence, not compliance proof.

Realistic production incident

A refresh token expired during a campaign. Twenty parallel API calls each refreshed independently; provider rotation marked reuse, some requests retried non-idempotent writes, and a remote flag increased rollout because analytics uploads were failing and the dashboard treated missing errors as success. Users oscillated signed-out/in; duplicate writes occurred. Containment: freeze rollout server-side, disable unsafe retry, fence affected sessions and reconcile operation IDs. Root cause: no single-flight/generation, 401/403/network collapsed into one error, and a telemetry-dependent positive feedback loop. Fix: one refresh coordinator, retry-once eligibility, server idempotency/status lookup, independent rollout guardrail, missing-telemetry alarm and control/data-plane isolation.

Code-review/design trap

Trap: singleton PlatformManager reads mutable currentUser, logs arbitrary event maps with bearer headers, calls fetch() and assumes activation, stores a provider secret in BuildConfig, refreshes every 401, and uses new_ui_enabled to bypass backend role checks. Tests are green. Block it: immutable generation-scoped context, typed separated interfaces/stores, token redaction and schemas, single-flight safe retry, validate+activate snapshot, no shipped secret, server authorization and privacy/contract/failure tests.

Likely practice Q&A

Це likely practice questions, не підтверджений і не гарантований список співбесіди.

  1. Q: Як розділити три subsystems? A: Auth owns session/identity context, analytics owns consented event pipeline, flags own typed policy snapshot; інтеграція лише через versioned context/contracts.
  2. Q: Що дає PKCE? A: Зв’язує code exchange з verifier і зменшує interception risk, але не замінює redirect/state/nonce/server validation.
  3. Q: Як обробити 20 одночасних 401? A: One single-flight refresh за token generation; safe callers retry once, інші reconcile/not retry.
  4. Q: 401, 403 і timeout? A: Authentication/session, authorization, transient network/service — різні стани й UX.
  5. Q: Чи biometric логінить backend? A: Ні, це local user-presence/key-use gate; backend session/authorization окремі.
  6. Q: Яка analytics delivery semantics? A: Bounded durable queue й at-least-once-oriented retry допускають loss/duplicate/reorder; exactly-once не обіцяємо.
  7. Q: Коли exposure event? A: Лише коли treatment реально exposed за визначеною межею, не під час fetch/assignment.
  8. Q: Fetch і activate? A: Fetch отримує candidate; validation+activate атомарно публікує snapshot, інакше LKG/default.
  9. Q: Чи flag може захистити admin action? A: Ні; UI flag не authorization, backend перевіряє principal/audience/scope/role.
  10. Q: Як робити account switch? A: Fence generation, cancel/clear old partition, не merge profiles, відкрити target session/flags/context.

Senior follow-ups

  1. Як ви формально визначите retry-safe endpoint і поведінку, якщо refresh succeeded, а original non-idempotent response lost?
  2. Як consent withdrawal проходить через local queue, ingestion, warehouse, derived tables і backups із auditable status?
  3. Як стабільний bucketing key переживає anonymous→signed-in без privacy-unsafe merge та sample contamination?
  4. Як kill switch працює при stale offline snapshot, а analytics control signal частково unavailable?

Unanswered self-checks

  1. Який компонент може атомарно змінити account/context generation і хто fence-ить старі callbacks?
  2. Які events/fields справді потрібні, для якої purpose, retention і deletion SLA?
  3. Які flag combinations невалідні та який safe behavior без control plane?
  4. Як довести, що outage analytics не автоматично прискорить небезпечний rollout?

English answer skeletons

30-second answer

“I separate auth, analytics, and flags into owned failure domains. Auth uses Authorization Code with PKCE in an external user-agent, verified redirects, short-lived access tokens, generation-aware single-flight refresh, account partitioning, and backend authorization. Analytics uses consented typed schemas, a bounded durable at-least-once-oriented queue, server validation, and no sensitive payloads. Flags use a typed registry, safe defaults, validated last-known-good snapshots, deterministic privacy-aware bucketing, and real exposure events. Startup publishes one consistent context; logout, account switch, consent change, offline state, and process death have explicit teardown and recovery.”

2-minute answer

“I start with ownership, journeys, privacy and failure boundaries. Identity, authentication, authorization, session, account and device are distinct. A native app uses OAuth Authorization Code plus PKCE through an external user-agent; state, nonce, verifier and exact verified redirect each have separate replay/tamper duties. The backend validates issuer, audience, scope and authorization. Access tokens are short-lived; concurrent 401s join one generation-aware refresh and eligible requests retry once, while 403 and transient network failures follow different paths. Tokens and all work are partitioned by account; biometric only gates local presence, Keystore has a bounded threat model, and no APK secret is trusted. Analytics events come from a versioned schema registry with required fields, pseudonymous context, purpose consent, minimization and PII controls. A bounded persistent queue batches under constraints with backoff and jitter; duplicate, late, reordered and lost events are expected, so ingestion validates and deduplicates without promising exactly-once or trusting source timestamps. Product analytics is separate from observability. Flags are typed with owner, default, expiry and dependencies. Fetch is not activation: validate a complete candidate and atomically publish it, otherwise use last-known-good or local defaults. Targeting rules may be client-visible; flags never authorize or hide secrets. Bucketing is deterministic but not proof of experiment validity, and exposure fires only when treatment is actually exposed. Startup loads defaults, account storage, session, consent and a validated snapshot before asynchronous refresh. Logout and account switch fence generations, cancel work and reset context; consent withdrawal stops collection and starts backend deletion. I test races, replay, process death, corruption, stale config and failure isolation, with independent rollout guardrails so missing analytics cannot look healthy.”

Official references

  • IETF RFC 8252 — OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps; RFC 7636 — PKCE; OpenID Connect Core; RFC 7009 — Token Revocation
  • Android Developers — Verify App Links; Android Keystore; Credential Manager; Passkeys; Biometric authentication
  • Firebase Analytics documentation; Analytics data collection and consent controls; Events
  • Firebase Remote Config for Android; Loading strategies; Real-time Remote Config; Firebase A/B Testing
  • Android security best practices; Privacy and security
Migration design: XML Views→Compose, RxJava→Flow/coroutines, modularization and safe deliveryрозгорнути / згорнути

Мета, discovery і senior mental model

Migration — не самоціль і не переписування «старого» на «нове», а керована зміна production-системи заради перевірюваного business outcome з обмеженим ризиком. Спочатку зафіксуйте business goals: швидкість доставки конкретних journeys, reliability, accessibility, talent/support cost, build/CI feedback або припинення unsupported dependency. Не оголошуйте Compose, Flow, Clean Architecture чи більше modules автоматичною ціллю.

Discovery створює baseline: pain/cost (lead time, defect/incident rate, crash/ANR/jank, test flakiness, clean/incremental/CI build time), dependency/build graph і critical path, runtime behavior/traces, data/state authorities, ownership/on-call, release cadence і installed-version tail, critical flows та compatibility constraints (min/target SDK, devices, accessibility/input, backend/schema, partner SDK, old clients). Позначте unsupported assumptions, невідомі side effects і дані без evidence. Визначте success criteria, guardrails, budget, stop/pivot criteria та deadline; не вигадуйте metrics — виміряйте current і target разом із product/SRE owners.

Стратегії міграції та винятки

СтратегіяКоли доречнаРизик
Big bang/rewriteМала ізольована система, короткий lifecycle, legal/vendor deadline або legacy неможливо безпечно змінювати; є повний parity lab і cutover planДовга divergence, інтеграція наприкінці, складний rollback
Branch by abstractionМожна поставити стабільний contract/adapter і переключати implementationТимчасова indirection, adapter стає permanent
Strangler / incremental vertical slicesLive product із незалежно вимірюваними user flowsMixed stack і bridge tax, зате малий blast radius
OpportunisticTouch-to-migrate біля змін із низьким ризикомНерівномірна topology, міграція може ніколи не завершитися

Default — reversible incremental vertical slices, не horizontal «переписати всі screens/operators/modules»: одна user capability проходить UI→state→domain/data→telemetry і може бути відключена без втрати даних. Big bang допустимий лише коли boundary справді малий, coexistence дорожче/небезпечніше, deadline жорсткий і rehearsal доводить cutover; opportunistic підхід потребує sunset backlog, інакше legacy не зникає.

Migration control plane

  • RFC/ADR: problem/evidence, alternatives, target та interim architecture, non-goals, compatibility, decision owner і date/revisit trigger.
  • Rules/map: allowed dependency directions, forbidden new legacy edges, current→interim→target topology; inventory/backlog by slice, owner, risk tier, dependencies, evidence and deletion gate.
  • Delivery: migration budget/capacity, risk-tier quality gates, telemetry dashboard, release cohort, deprecation policy/deadline and escalation for exceptions.
  • Checkpoints: go/hold/rollback/roll-forward decision before merge, activation, cohort growth and legacy deletion; named incident commander and rollback owner.
  • Exit: bridge usage reaches zero, legacy dependency/build wiring/flags removed, docs/on-call updated, outcomes measured. Migration complete means legacy dependencies/bridges/flags are removed and outcomes verified, not merely new code added.

Dependency/topology diagram

                  RFC/ADR + migration map + risk gates + telemetry
                                      │
App composition root / Nav host ──────┼──────── release flag (routing only)
        │                             │
 legacy Fragment/XML ─ ComposeView ─ new plain Compose UI
        │                    \         ↑ state + callbacks
 AndroidView/Binding ←──────── Compose route/state holder
        └──────────── one state owner / one navigation / one analytics authority
                                      │
 UI state holder → authoritative use case/repository contract
              Rx façade ⇄ tested adapter boundary ⇄ Flow/suspend pipeline
                                      │
      data/API/DB authority (expand → migrate/backfill → contract)

Gradle dependency direction: :app(composition root) → feature API
 feature implementation → narrow platform/data APIs; no reverse edge/cycle
Telemetry compares old/new outcomes; rollout can route back only while data/contracts remain compatible.

Migration-slice template

  • Outcome/scope: user journey and business goal; explicit non-goals.
  • Baseline: current runtime trace, owner, dependencies, cost/quality metrics, critical states and characterization tests.
  • Semantics: source of truth, lifecycle/scope, threading/cancellation/error/backpressure, restore/navigation/analytics, accessibility and compatibility contracts.
  • Change: old/interim/target topology, adapters, public API/resources/schema changes, ownership and deletion issue.
  • Risk/delivery: tier, flag limits, dark/shadow policy, cohorts, guardrails, halt threshold, rollback and roll-forward including irreversible state.
  • Evidence/exit: tests, dashboards, parity sample, support/runbook; remove old route, bridge, flag and dependency only after observation window.

XML Views→Compose: interop і lifecycle

Мігруйте leaf або повну screen boundary, а не вкладайте View↔Compose↔View лише для migration convenience. У View/Fragment вставляйте ComposeView, задайте stable ID для saved state за потреби, встановіть content після коректних LifecycleOwner/SavedStateRegistryOwner/ViewModelStoreOwner, і виберіть ViewCompositionStrategy відповідно до host lifecycle (для Fragment view lifecycle зазвичай disposal on destroyed lifecycle). Неправильний owner/strategy дає retained composition, double collectors або disposed UI; перевіряйте recreation, back stack і leak traces.

У Compose використовуйте AndroidView для View та AndroidViewBinding для XML/ViewBinding; factory створює instance, update ідемпотентно синхронізує актуальні props, cleanup/listeners мають симетричний disposal/release. Не кешуйте View поза factory без доведеного ownership, не запускайте analytics/network у update, не створюйте Fragment довільно всередині AndroidView. Для Fragment-in-Compose дотримуйтесь офіційного interop container/FragmentManager ownership і унікальних IDs; version-sensitive API перевіряйте в pinned Compose/Fragment/Nav docs.

Compose: state, restoration, navigation і UX parity

Розділіть route/state-holder composable (ViewModel/DI, lifecycle-aware collection, effects/navigation) і plain UI composable (immutable state + callbacks). На slice має бути one state owner; View і Compose не підтримують дві mutable copies. Так само рівно один owner для navigation, analytics impression і user action. remember переживає recomposition, rememberSaveable — лише saveable boundary та не є durable storage; business state відновлюється з repository/SavedStateHandle за contract. Визначте IDs/keys і restoration behavior до cutover.

Під час Fragment/Nav coexistence route залишається на одному back stack; Compose надсилає callbacks, host виконує navigation, поки destination не мігрована цілком. Узгодьте Material/View theme tokens, typography, density, dark/high contrast, content descriptions/semantics, traversal/focus, keyboard/D-pad, IME, window insets, system bars, dialogs і back. RecyclerView→lazy list: stable item identity/content type, anchor ID+offset, selection/focus and pagination state; index alone не переживає reorder. Не дублюйте state, analytics чи navigation в обох деревах.

Compose: performance, tests і limitations

Characterize old UI first. Перевіряйте unit/state tests, semantics/a11y, screenshot/golden на representative fonts/themes/sizes, navigation/restoration/process recreation, View↔Compose integration та baseline/macrobenchmark startup/scroll/jank у release/profileable builds. Compose does not inherently make UI faster; compare measured frame timing, allocations and critical interactions. Baseline Profiles допомагають compilation paths, але не виправляють expensive composition/layout або wrong state reads. Preview корисний для plain UI states, але не доводить runtime lifecycle, DI/Nav, resources/configuration, IME/insets, accessibility service, animation timing чи device rendering.

Compiling interop does not prove lifecycle/state/accessibility parity. Screenshot parity не доводить semantics/focus; semantics tests не доводять pixels/performance. Тестуйте disposal при detach/re-attach, Fragment view recreation і pool/reuse; шукайте listener/owner/composition leaks. Interop layer має owner, telemetry і deletion date.

RxJava→Flow/coroutines: semantic inventory before conversion

До коду складіть inventory кожного pipeline: Single/Maybe/Completable/Observable/Flowable, cold/hot/connectable, subscriber count/replay, empty/null/error contract, completion, ordering/concurrency, retry, timeout, scheduler boundaries, backpressure strategy, disposal side effects і scope owner. There is no safe universal 1:1 operator mapping; mechanical rename приховує semantic regressions. suspend найчастіше відповідає one-shot result, Flow — stream, але Maybe empty, Completable completion, nullability та terminal errors потребують explicit domain type/contract.

Bridge тимчасово через pinned/tested kotlinx-coroutines-rx2/rx3 adapters або вузький власний adapter; лише один authoritative pipeline виконує I/O/cache/write/analytics. Забороніть Rx subscribes to Flow that also feeds Rx back. Кожна mixed Rx/coroutine boundary потребує tests cancellation в обидва боки, error/completion/empty, disposal cleanup, threading і double-subscription.

Flow/coroutines semantic map

  • Cancellation: Rx Disposable сигналізує dispose за contract оператора; coroutine cancellation cooperative — blocking/non-cancellable code має реагувати/бути bounded. Structured concurrency: caller/UI state holder owns scope; repositories переважно expose suspend/Flow, не hidden fire-and-forget scope.
  • CoroutineContext: subscribeOn/observeOn не замінюються глобальним dispatcher. withContext зміщує suspend block; flowOn впливає лише upstream і зберігає context preservation downstream. Документуйте main-safety.
  • Errors: Flow має exception transparency; catch ловить upstream, не downstream collector. Не ковтайте CancellationException. retry/retryWhen повторно запускають upstream і можуть повторити side effects — потрібні eligibility/idempotency/backoff.
  • Rate mismatch: Flow за замовчуванням suspends producer/collector chain; це не universal equivalent Rx Flowable strategies. buffer, conflate, collectLatest, drop policies змінюють гарантії й мають бути explicit.
  • Composition: combine використовує latest після першого value кожного input; merge interleaves; zip pairs; flatMapLatest cooperative-cancels previous. Вони не взаємозамінні.
  • Hotness/events: StateFlow — conflated current state з initial value, не event log; SharedFlow задає replay/buffer/broadcast; Channel.receiveAsFlow() fan-out delivers element одному consumer, не broadcast. Delivery across no collector/process death не магічна — model durable state/queue when required.
  • Lifecycle/callbacks: UI uses repeatOnLifecycle/collectAsStateWithLifecycle as appropriate. repeatOnLifecycle stops/restarts collection but does not fix wrong upstream scope/sharing. callbackFlow реєструє callback і обов’язково awaitClose unregisters; handle trySend failure.

Virtual-time tests use runTest, shared TestCoroutineScheduler, test dispatchers and explicit runCurrent/advanceTimeBy/advanceUntilIdle; assert cancellation, retry delays, latest cancellation, hot replay and no leftover jobs. Virtual time не моделює real blocking/thread races.

Legacy modularization: boundary before module

Розрізняйте: package cleanup (namespace лише), source-set/source module, Gradle module (compilation/dependency boundary) і Play dynamic feature (delivery/install boundary). Обирайте boundary за ownership, cohesion, change coupling, public capability, dependency/build graph і deploy/test needs — не за layer diagram чи target module count. Спершу package/API seam і dependency inversion там, де вона справді розриває policy from mechanism; потім extraction, якщо evidence виправдовує cost.

Визначте narrow public API, api vs implementation, dependency direction та composition root. DI wiring, navigation contracts, resources/themes, manifests, database/entity/migration and network DTO ownership мають явного owner; app/composition root збирає implementations. Забороніть cycles, reverse implementation edges і :common/:shared dumping ground. Binary/source/resource compatibility різні: зміна public signature/default/inline/type, Java/Kotlin interop або resource name/theme/manifest може ламати consumers; version/capability contracts і staged source moves потрібні навіть у monorepo.

Build, compatibility і version guidance

Module extraction does not automatically improve build time and may worsen configuration/critical path. Baseline та порівняння: clean, ABI-compatible incremental, implementation change, resource change, IDE sync і representative CI cache/parallel critical path; профілюйте Gradle/Build Analyzer/scan перед/після. Version catalogs і convention plugins централізують versions/build policy, але є enablers not architecture і можуть розширити invalidation, якщо зроблені монолітом.

Version-sensitive: pin Android Gradle Plugin, Gradle, Kotlin, Compose BOM/compiler plugin, Lifecycle, Navigation, Fragment, RecyclerView, coroutines, RxJava та rx interop adapters; читайте їх release notes/migration docs. Не переносіть current ViewCompositionStrategy, typed navigation, strong skipping, baseline-profile, K2 або dynamic-feature assumptions на іншу pinned version. Update one compatibility axis per rehearsed slice when possible, run consumer/build/plugin tests, and keep an ADR of verified combinations. Android API/device/OEM behavior and old installed clients remain runtime constraints.

Safe delivery and data evolution

Перед refactor додайте characterization tests навколо critical behavior; де корисно — golden, contract, screenshot, accessibility, migration і performance tests. Dark launch/shadow read має порівнювати side-effect-free або sandboxed output; shadow traffic can create side effects/privacy/cost, тому redaction, consent, rate limits, isolation і deletion policy обов’язкові. Feature flag може route implementation, але не виправляє duplicated pipeline і feature flags do not roll back incompatible persisted data.

Staged rollout: internal→canary cohorts→small production→growth із crash/ANR/jank, latency/error, data parity та business guardrails; halt criteria й owner наперед. Staged rollout limits blast radius but doesn't prove safety or instantly remove installed versions. Database/network/schema evolution — expand→migrate/backfill→contract: спершу additive tolerant readers/writers/server support, потім measured migration, і лише після old-client tail/compatibility evidence видаляйте old field/path. Dual-read/write потребують authority, deterministic compare/reconciliation, divergence metric and deadline; dual-write has no atomic cross-system guarantee. Не робіть обидві сторони authority.

Rollback must be designed before rollout. DB migrations, server contracts, destructive writes або privacy deletion можуть бути irreversible; тоді plan — roll-forward/repair, не APK rollback. Feature flags не повертають persisted bytes/schema. Після observation window cleanup gate видаляє old code/dependency/module edge, adapter, flag, telemetry branch, compatibility write and runbook debt.

Sequence: one realistic vertical slice

  1. Оберіть низько-/середньоризиковий «saved items» flow без payment/auth authority; baseline behavior, scroll/focus, Rx semantics, build graph і metrics.
  2. Characterize repository contract, UI state transitions, empty/error/retry, navigation, analytics and DB schema; зафіксуйте ADR, risk and rollback.
  3. Створіть one authoritative suspend/Flow pipeline behind existing interface; Rx adapter keeps old screen alive. Mixed-boundary tests prove cancellation/error/empty/threading.
  4. Виділіть plain state-driven Compose content; host it in existing Fragment via ComposeView with correct view lifecycle strategy. Fragment owns Nav; ViewModel owns state; one analytics path.
  5. Preserve stable item IDs and list anchor; test recreation, process restoration, a11y/focus/IME/insets, screenshots and macrobenchmark parity.
  6. Route a canary cohort, compare old/new operational and business outcomes; halt on guardrail breach. If data compatible, route back; otherwise roll forward repair.
  7. Grow rollout, observe installed-version tail, then remove XML/Rx adapter/flag/unused dependency. Re-measure build/runtime goals and close only after outcomes verified.

Risk register / failure matrix

FailureDetectionContainment / repair
Compose composition survives Fragment viewLeak trace, duplicate collection after back stackCorrect owner/strategy; dispose and regression recreation test
View and Compose both own state/nav/analyticsDuplicate event/navigation, divergent UIOne authority; adapter is projection only
Lazy list loses anchor/focusParity/session replay, accessibility testStable ID+offset and deterministic fallback
Rx→Flow changes empty/error/retryContract + virtual-time boundary testsExplicit result type; revert adapter route
Cancellation swallowedJob remains active, duplicate writesRethrow cancellation, caller-owned scope, reconcile effects
Hot stream wrong replay/fan-outRotation/multi-collector event loss/duplicateChoose StateFlow/SharedFlow/Channel/durable queue by contract
New module creates cycle/build regressionDependency rule + clean/incremental/CI profileMove composition root/API; merge/revert boundary if no value
Shadow path writes/exports dataAudit/cost/side-effect alarmsKill shadow, isolate sandbox, purge per policy
Dual writes divergeReconciliation mismatch/ageFreeze cutover, authoritative repair/backfill
Rollback app cannot read new DB/server stateDowngrade/old-client contract testsHalt rollout; roll forward compatible reader/repair
Canary green, broad cohort failsSegmented crash/ANR/jank/business metricsStop growth, cohort-aware disable, incident runbook

Guarantees and explicit non-guarantees

  • Compiling interop does not prove lifecycle/state/accessibility parity.
  • Compose does not inherently make UI faster.
  • Flow is not drop-in Rx and StateFlow is not an event log; cancellation is cooperative.
  • repeatOnLifecycle stops/restarts collection but does not fix wrong upstream scope/sharing.
  • Feature flags do not roll back incompatible persisted data.
  • Staged rollout limits blast radius but doesn't prove safety or instantly remove installed versions.
  • Tests and CI green do not prove production parity.
  • Modularization does not automatically speed builds or enforce ownership.
  • Shadow traffic can create side effects/privacy/cost.
  • Dual-write has no atomic cross-system guarantee.
  • Rollback must be designed before rollout.
  • Migration complete means legacy dependencies/bridges/flags are removed and outcomes verified, not merely new code added.

Decision framework

  1. Назвіть outcome, baseline, constraints, unsupported assumptions і stop criteria.
  2. Картуйте runtime/build/dependency/data topology, authorities, owners, critical flows and installed-version tail.
  3. Оберіть найменший vertical seam; порівняйте no migration, opportunistic, abstraction/strangler та big bang.
  4. Для UI/async/modules окремо зафіксуйте semantics, lifecycle, compatibility, interop tax і deletion gate.
  5. Спроєктуйте evidence, telemetry, data compatibility, rollout/rollback/roll-forward до implementation.
  6. На checkpoints grow/hold/pivot; закрийте лише після deletion legacy and measured outcomes.

Trade-offs and evolution

Малі slices знижують blast radius, але довше оплачують mixed-stack adapters; великі slices скорочують coexistence, але концентрують unknowns. Stable abstraction полегшує routing, але може зацементувати найгірший legacy contract. UI parity уповільнює visual redesign, зате відділяє migration risk від product change. Dual-read дає evidence, але коштує latency/privacy; dual-write підвищує divergence risk. Більше modules може покращити ownership/parallel compilation лише за правильного graph, інакше додає configuration/ABI/resource edges. Еволюціонуйте one dimension at a time, переглядайте ADR на evidence checkpoints і budget adapters як тимчасовий debt.

Observability and testing plan

Дашборд сегментує implementation/cohort/app version/device: route exposure, crash/ANR, jank/frame time, startup, memory/leaks, a11y failures where measurable, navigation/restore errors, cancellation/retry/duplicate side effects, Rx/Flow adapter use, data divergence/backfill age, build clean/incremental/CI critical path, business conversion/completion and support contacts. Privacy-safe correlation links route version to outcome; missing telemetry is unknown, not success.

Testing pyramid by risk: characterization/unit/property tests; Rx↔coroutine contract and runTest virtual time; DB/network/schema/old-client and downgrade compatibility; Fragment/View/Compose integration and process recreation; semantics/focus/IME/insets/screenshot; macrobenchmark/baseline profile; staged production synthetic and canary evidence. Tests and CI green do not prove production parity, so checkpoints use both lab and runtime evidence.

Realistic production incident

Команда мігрувала search Fragment: ComposeView retained composition довше Fragment view, а Rx source і новий stateIn(applicationScope) обидва виконували search. Після rotation два collectors писали history і analytics; flatMapLatest не зупиняв blocking legacy call, тому старі results іноді перемагали. Canary був green через низьку rotation rate, broad rollout підняв duplicate events і jank. Containment: зупинили rollout, route повернули на old UI, але залишили additive schema; відключили new writer і reconciled duplicate history. Root cause: механічне operator mapping, wrong scope/sharing, duplicate authority і неправильна composition strategy. Fix: Fragment-view lifecycle disposal, one pipeline behind adapter, cancellable/bounded bridge, request generation guard, rotation/cancellation tests і cohort telemetry.

Code-review/design trap

Trap: PR додає ComposeView у RecyclerView item, усередині AndroidView inflate-ить старий layout, обидві сторони collect-ять Rx і StateFlow, GlobalScope bridge ковтає errors, navigation та analytics викликаються двічі, а новий :common module експортує все. «Компілюється і screenshots схожі» — не acceptance. Block: одна meaningful UI boundary, one state/nav/analytics owner, explicit lifecycle strategy, tested cancellation/error bridge, narrow API/dependency direction, parity/performance/a11y evidence і deletion issue.

Likely practice Q&A

Це likely practice questions, не підтверджений і не гарантований список співбесіди.

  1. Q: З чого почати migration? A: З business outcome, measured pain, topology/owners/constraints, unsupported assumptions, success і stop criteria.
  2. Q: Big bang чи incremental? A: Default reversible vertical slices; big bang лише для малого ізольованого boundary з rehearsal і нижчим coexistence risk.
  3. Q: Як вставити Compose у Fragment? A: ComposeView зі свідомим lifecycle/save-state ownership і ViewCompositionStrategy; перевірити recreation/disposal/leaks.
  4. Q: Як вставити View у Compose? A: AndroidView/AndroidViewBinding із factory/update/cleanup contracts, без side effects у update.
  5. Q: Як не дублювати UI behavior? A: One state, navigation and analytics authority; plain UI receives state/callbacks, bridge тільки projects.
  6. Q: Чи є Rx→Flow operator table? A: Немає safe universal 1:1 mapping; inventory hot/cold/error/empty/backpressure/cancellation first.
  7. Q: StateFlow для events? A: Ні, це current conflated state, не event log; replay/fan-out/durability model explicit.
  8. Q: Коли створювати Gradle module? A: Коли ownership/cohesion/dependency/build evidence виправдовує compile/config/API cost, не заради package cleanup.
  9. Q: Чи flag гарантує rollback? A: Лише route compatible code; не відкотить DB/schema/server side effects.
  10. Q: Коли migration done? A: Outcomes verified і old route, adapters, dependencies, flags та temporary telemetry removed.

Senior follow-ups

  1. Як ви мігруєте checkout screen, якщо DB write нового client не читає попередня installed version?
  2. Спроєктуйте Rx↔Flow bridge для hot replaying source з двома collectors і cancellation у обидва боки.
  3. Як довести RecyclerView→LazyColumn scroll/focus/a11y parity під reorder і process recreation?
  4. Які build experiments покажуть, чи extraction feature module покращила representative CI critical path?

Unanswered self-checks

  1. Яка одна authority виконує side effect під час coexistence, і як технічно заборонений duplicate path?
  2. Який persisted/server state зробить rollback неможливим і який roll-forward repair?
  3. Які exact cohort guardrails зупиняють rollout, хто має право рішення і що означає missing telemetry?
  4. Який deletion gate доводить, що bridge/flag/module edge справді більше не потрібний?

English answer skeletons

30-second answer

“I treat migration as an outcomes-and-risk program, not a rewrite goal. I baseline business pain, runtime and build topology, ownership, critical flows, compatibility and stop criteria. I default to reversible vertical slices with one state and side-effect authority. Compose/View and Rx/coroutine bridges are temporary, lifecycle- and semantics-tested boundaries. Data evolves expand-migrate-contract, rollout uses cohort guardrails, and rollback is designed before activation. The work is complete only when legacy bridges, flags and dependencies are removed and outcomes are verified.”

2-minute answer

“I begin with discovery: the business outcome, measured cost, dependency and build graph, runtime behavior, owners, release cadence, installed-version tail, critical journeys, compatibility constraints, unsupported assumptions, success and stop criteria. I compare doing nothing, opportunistic change, branch by abstraction, strangler slices and a big bang; for a live product I normally choose a reversible vertical slice because it limits blast radius and produces evidence early. An RFC/ADR defines target and interim architecture, dependency rules, risk tier, owner, budget, quality gates, telemetry, deprecation and rollback or roll-forward checkpoints. For XML to Compose I place one meaningful interop boundary, choose ComposeView lifecycle/disposal deliberately or AndroidView factory/update/cleanup deliberately, retain one state/navigation/analytics owner, and prove restoration, accessibility, focus, IME, insets, list identity, screenshot and measured performance parity. For Rx to Flow I inventory hot/cold, empty/null/error/completion, scheduler, retry, backpressure, replay/fan-out and disposal before converting; there is no universal operator mapping, cancellation is cooperative, and every mixed boundary gets cancellation and error tests. For modules I choose boundaries by ownership, cohesion and the measured graph, define narrow APIs and a composition root, and profile clean, incremental and CI builds. Data uses expand-migrate-contract; shadow traffic is isolated; canaries have crash, ANR, jank, data and business guardrails. Flags cannot undo incompatible data, so rollback is designed first and irreversible cases have a roll-forward repair. Finally I remove old routes, adapters, flags and dependencies and remeasure the outcome.”

Official references

  • Android Developers — Compose migration strategy; Compose in Views; Views in Compose; Testing migration
  • Save UI state in Compose; Compose accessibility; Compose Baseline Profiles
  • Android coroutines best practices; Kotlin Flow; Coroutine cancellation; kotlinx-coroutines-test
  • RxJava 3 Javadoc; kotlinx-coroutines-rx3 adapters
  • Android app modularization guide; Optimize build speed; Profile your build
Stage 32 — Senior engineering practice: review, mentorship, decisions, stakeholders and trade-offs (фінальний етап гайда)розгорнути / згорнути

Мета, межа і senior scope проти title

Stage 32 — фінальний етап цього гайда. Після нього немає етапів 33–35 і немає вигаданих mock-interview chapters. Мета — показати interview-ready senior practice як операційну систему: зменшувати неоднозначність, технічно виконувати складне, впливати без формальної влади, покращувати system/team outcomes і тримати sustainable pace. Seniority — не кількість років і не title сам по собі. Очікування від Senior, Lead і Staff залежать від організації, її масштабу, продукту та ladder; універсальної promotion ladder немає. В одній компанії Lead координує delivery і людей, Staff працює cross-team; в іншій ці назви означають інше. На співбесіді уточнюйте scope, decision rights і expected outcomes, а не вгадуйте назву.

Senior не «володіє всім»: він робить ownership явним, піднімає ризик із evidence та options, ескалює до того, хто має authority, і знає, коли не будувати платформу. Якщо reversible локальний patch з observability та expiry дешевший за general framework — over-engineering є ризиком. Sustainable pace означає керовану capacity, чергування on-call, timeboxes і зменшення повторної роботи, а не героїчні ночі як process.

Operating model: від неоднозначності до evidence

  1. Frame: хто користувач/decision owner, який outcome, deadline, constraints, non-goals і що невідомо.
  2. Map: affected groups, authorities, dependencies, failure cost, reversible/irreversible effects і residual risk.
  3. Choose: варіанти включно з «нічого не робити»; evidence, assumptions, confidence, recommendation, owner і decision deadline.
  4. Deliver: vertical slices, guardrails, checkpoints, observability, rollout/rollback або roll-forward.
  5. Learn: перевірити outcome після release, оновити ADR/risk/debt register, закрити follow-ups. Activity (PR count, meetings, mentoring hours) не дорівнює impact.

Escalation test: ескалюйте не тому, що є disagreement, а коли risk перевищує вашу authority/tolerance, deadline блокується, owner відсутній, compliance/security duty порушується або потрібне cross-team allocation. Принесіть короткий контекст, evidence, already-tried, options, recommendation, decision needed by і наслідок delay.

Code review як risk-control і learning loop

Цілі review: correctness, security, maintainability і learning. Review не може довести correctness/security; CI також не доводить production safety. Глибина має відповідати ризику: auth/payment/data migration/concurrency/public API потребують invariants, abuse cases, rollback і domain reviewer; low-risk copy/config може мати коротший шлях. Автор робить change малим і reviewable, описує why/scope/non-goals/risk, self-review, tests/evidence, rollout і migrations. Reviewer читає context, перевіряє design/data/security/failure/testability, запускає або просить потрібне evidence, чітко володіє чергою та не затримує change мовчанням.

  • Коментарі: label BLOCKING, NON-BLOCKING, QUESTION, SUGGESTION, NIT; поясніть risk/why, запропонуйте direction або test. Критикуйте code/behavior, не людину. Питання не маскує наказ; suggestion не маскує block.
  • Approval semantics: «approve» означає «за переглянутим scope і evidence не бачу blocking issue», а не гарантію безпеки чи довічну підтримку design. Автор лишається owner merge/rollout; reviewer відповідає за добросовісну review.
  • Latency/ownership: домовтеся про primary reviewer, risk experts і очікуваний response window; acknowledge швидко, review малими batches, reassign/ескалуйте, якщо не можете. Speed важлива, але не виправдовує rubber stamp.
  • Disagreement: сформулюйте shared goal та decision owner; відділіть standard/invariant від preference; time-box sync/spike; зафіксуйте decision. Після decision — disagree-and-commit, крім нової security/compliance evidence.

Антипатерни: rubber stamp, review лише nits, architecture-by-comment після великого PR, вимога клонувати reviewer style, нескінченна дискусія без owner/deadline, surprise redesign, і approval на green CI без читання failure modes. Великі зміни спершу потребують RFC/design sync, не архітектури, винайденої у 80 comments.

Template: severity для code-review comment

[BLOCKING | NON-BLOCKING | QUESTION | SUGGESTION | NIT]
Observed: <конкретний code/behavior>
Impact/risk: <correctness, security, operability, maintenance, learning>
Evidence/assumption: <test, trace, contract або невідоме>
Requested next action: <change/test/clarification; example direction>
Scope: <цей PR | follow-up owner + date>

Приклад без персональної атаки: BLOCKING — два collectors можуть списати одну outbox row. Додайте atomic claim test або поясніть DB invariant. Не пишіть «ти знову не розумієш concurrency».

Mentorship, feedback, delegation і sponsorship

Почніть із діагностики: мета людини, current model, контекст, stakes, бажаний рівень autonomy і constraints. Оберіть режим: pairing для спільного discovery/високого ризику; Socratic questions коли learner має базу й може побудувати judgment; direct instruction для incident, hard constraint або відсутньої foundational knowledge. Не перетворюйте Socratic method на загадки. Scaffolding: demonstrate → do together → learner owns bounded slice → learner owns decision/delivery → mentor доступний у checkpoints; поступово знімайте опори.

Feedback: behavior → impact → next action, конкретно і близько до події: «У status update не було decision deadline; backend не зарезервував capacity; наступного разу додай owner/date і dependency». Psychological safety означає можливість ставити питання, визнавати помилки й dissent без приниження; вона не означає уникати прямого feedback або знижувати standards. Delegation передає execution/decision space з outcome, context, constraints, authority, guardrails, checkpoints і escalation triggers; accountability делегатора не зникає.

Mentorship розвиває skill/judgment; sponsorship використовує власний вплив, щоб створити видимість, доступ і можливість, називаючи внесок людини. Вимірюйте outcomes: більша незалежність, якість рішень, прогнозовані escalation, ownership складнішого slice, feedback від collaborators — не кількість зустрічей. Не забирайте credit. Уникайте bottleneck («усе через мене»), cloning власного стилю, unsolicited rescue і виконання задачі замість learner.

Template: mentorship/delegation plan

Goal and learner context: <перевірити разом; не припускати>
Evidence of current capability: <observed behavior/work sample>
Target behavior/outcome by <date/checkpoint>: <...>
Mode: pairing | Socratic | direct instruction — why: <...>
Delegated scope + decision rights: <...>
Constraints/guardrails: <security, quality, time, people>
Checkpoints and escalation triggers: <...>
Feedback: behavior → impact → next action
Success evidence / next ownership step: <...>
Credit/sponsorship action: <хто має побачити внесок learner>

Decision practice: doors, owner, evidence і learning

Спочатку визначте reversibility. Two-way door — дешево й швидко відкотити з обмеженим blast radius; делегуйте і вирішуйте швидше. One-way door — legal/public API/irreversible data або дорогий lock-in; більше evidence, security/legal/domain input і rehearsal. Це spectrum: feature flag не робить irreversible state reversible. Для кожного рішення вкажіть decision owner, потрібний input, deadline; consensus не завжди потрібен. Input — не veto за замовчуванням.
